shared_elements: incised/carved linear motifs on a stone surface
horizontal line bearing a row of short repeated strokes (comb-like hatching)
justification: The only real correspondence is the generic device of a line carrying a row of short repeated strokes (crew-strokes or hull hatching in A, garment fringe and hem borders in B), plus stacked roughly horizontal linear motifs; this is a motif any carving tradition could arrive at independently. Otherwise the depicted content diverges completely: A shows purely schematic outline forms with no identifiable figures or objects held, while B shows two large naturalistic, modelled human figures in profile facing one another, bearded and elaborately coiffed, one holding a bowl and gesturing, with fields of dense inscription-like signs.
